safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes lip/upper lip swelling but does not state duration as 'past 1 hour' (no equivalent duration documented).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In suspected anaphylaxis, documenting the time course (e.g., onset within ~1 hour) helps assess severity and guides urgency/ED handoff, but the presence of progressive lip swelling and respiratory symptoms already drives emergent management. The omission mainly reduces clinical context for downstream clinicians rather than changing immediate action.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold fact of an initial 'weird sensation around the lips' is not captured in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: An initial “weird sensation” around the lips is a nonspecific prodromal symptom and is less clinically actionable than objective swelling or breathing difficulty. Omitting it is unlikely to change diagnosis or management when more critical anaphylaxis features are present.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes shortness of breath but does not document a 'throat closing' sensation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A sensation of throat closing is a high-risk red-flag symptom suggestive of upper-airway involvement in anaphylaxis; failing to document it can lead to under-triage or less aggressive airway planning during handoff. Even with documented shortness of breath, this omission can meaningfully affect perceived severity and urgency.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No dizziness is mentioned in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can indicate systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension) in anaphylaxis and contributes to severity assessment and monitoring needs. If omitted, clinicians may underestimate reaction severity, though other serious features (lip swelling/respiratory complaints) still prompt emergency care.
